summary: Prefabricated 66-foot wooden tower on Cumberland Mountain near Ewing, Lee County, Virginia, reported new in July 1938; now listed as gone.

facts.design: Prefabricated wooden tower, 66 feet, with an 8 by 8 foot cabin on top
facts.agency: State of Virginia (tower described as state property)
facts.status_note: Listed as removed; no source gives a removal date or describes the site today

events.note: Newspaper report of July 16, 1938 describes a recently constructed prefabricated wooden tower on Cumberland Mountain

evidence.supports: 66-foot tower recently built on Cumberland Mountain, north of Ewing
evidence.quote: A 66-foot lookout tower has recently been constructed on Cumberland Mountain, just north of Ewing

evidence.supports: prefabricated wooden tower assembled from blueprints
evidence.quote: It is a complete wooden tower, pre-fabricated, and assembled according to blue prints.

evidence.supports: built by the local Forestry Service branch with TVA
evidence.quote: The work was done by the local branch of the U.S. Forestry Service, in co-operation with the T.V.A.

evidence.supports: CCC camp built the mountain trail
evidence.quote: A good mountain trail was built several months ago by the CCC camp
Mr. Powell, project Superintendent of the Jonesville CCC camp

evidence.supports: 8 by 8 foot cabin and view of about 20 miles
evidence.quote: On top of the tower is an 8 by 8 foot cabin, from which the surrounding area of about 20 miles radius, will be visible on clear days.

evidence.supports: state property; lookout to be appointed by the state
evidence.quote: The tower is the property of the State of Virginia, and a man will be appointed by the state to serve as lookout for forest fires.

evidence.supports: earlier geodetic survey use and signal lights
evidence.quote: The site upon which the tower is built has been used for several years, in making the geodetic surveys of the U.S., and the signal lights were visible at distant points in Kentucky and Tennessee

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts marks the tower removed
Forest Fire Lookout Association lists White Rock (Lee) as gone
evidence.quote: White Rock Lee / Harlan (KY) 36.66512 -83.45197 Tower Gone

notes_for_editor: Only two sources: a 1938 newspaper item (Middlesboro Daily News, as quoted by Forest Lookouts) and one line in the Forest Fire Lookout Association Virginia index. Two web searches for a Lee County or Cumberland Mountain tower found nothing further. No staffing, fire history, removal date or site description found; the 1938 article says a lookout would be appointed but does not confirm one was. The 'Harlan (KY)' county in the index is kept as printed. Do not confuse with us-va-white-rock (White Rock on Mill Mountain, Bath County), which is a different tower. The story is short because the evidence is thin.
